extracted.intended_audience: ICML authors, Program Chairs, Senior Area Chairs, Area Chairs, and Reviewers (ICML 2026 program committee and submitting authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Conference-specific ethical standards and procedural rules for submitting papers to ICML 2026 and for the behavior of the program committee (Program Chairs, Senior Area Chairs, Area Chairs, Reviewers). Covers author responsibilities, program-committee responsibilities, disclosures, LLM use, prompt-injection, and grounds for desk rejection and sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No interference with the peer-review process
rubrics_metrics.description: It is strictly forbidden to interfere with the peer-review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include collusion, creation of fake identities, misrepresenting publication history or biographical details, declaring unsubstantiated conflicts, or submission of low-quality AI-generated content ("AI slop"). Interference also includes attempts to uncover reviewer/meta-reviewer identities. Such behavior may lead to sanctions including desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should comprise exactly those individuals who made a significant contribution to the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other contributors should be acknowledged upon acceptance in the camera-ready. The submitting author must ensure all co-authors have seen and approved the final manuscript and agreed to submission. The author list cannot be changed after the abstract deadline (see Call for Papers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and appropriate citations
rubrics_metrics.description: The submitted paper must be entirely written by the authors and must properly cite or quote any work of others used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publications that significantly influenced the work must be cited. Only relevant publications should be cited and self-citation should be minimized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of concurrent research (timeliness exception and preprints)
rubrics_metrics.description: Works made public less than two months before the full-paper deadline are not required (but welcome) to be discussed; they should generally be viewed as independent (concurrent) research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: a preprint of the ICML submission is not treated as concurrent in this sense. If concurrent work has overlapping authors with the submission, follow dual/concurrent-submission rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual and concurrent submissions policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Concurrent submissions to ICML with an overlapping set of authors are considered prior work and must be handled accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a concurrent submission is on a related research topic normally included in related work, it must be discussed and cited in the body of the paper, and an anonymized PDF of the concurrent submission must be provided in the supplementary material. Failure to cite/discuss related concurrent submissions is considered abuse and may lead to desk rejection of the violating submission or of all submissions with the same authors, even if substantively different.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fraud and fabricated data prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Fraudulent or knowingly inaccurate statements are unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including but not limited to the use of fabricated data. Such conduct is grounds for sanctions and rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correctness / error disclosure obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: If before final publication an author discovers a significant error or inaccuracy in the submitted paper, they must promptly notify program chairs and either retract the paper or correct it if feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt notification to program-chairs@icml.cc is required; failure to do so is unethical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt injection prohibition (authors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any attempts at prompt injection by authors are forbidden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt injection refers to inserting specially crafted text into the paper with the intent to manipulate LLMs (e.g., to obtain favorable reviews). Update (2/14/2026): prompt injection by authors is disallowed, but prompts that merely seek to detect LLM use by reviewers will not be penalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial and substantive conflict-of-interest disclosure (authors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must disclose any financial or other substantive conflicts that could reasonably be perceived to influence the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include industry funding for work that evaluates or promotes the funder’s product/system/technology. Disclosures are visible to program chairs and the integrity chair (not to reviewers/ACs/SACs). Program chairs may share limited details with others if relevant while preserving author anonymity. Upon acceptance, authors must include a brief statement summarizing relevant conflicts and sources of financial support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind review and anonymization
rubrics_metrics.description: ICML uses double-blind reviewing; authors are required to anonymize submissions as outlined in the Call for Papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any attempts by authors to uncover identities of reviewers or meta-reviewers are forbidden and may also violate the Code of Conduct (doxxing). Violations of anonymity can be grounds for desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program committee: aims and goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Program committee members must strive to meet expectations/needs of conference participants, readers, and authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants and readers expect a high-quality, intellectually stimulating program; authors expect a fair and professional review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality for program committee members
rubrics_metrics.description: All information pertaining to submitted manuscripts must be kept confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program committee members and reviewers must protect authors' ideas and not disclose manuscript details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness in evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions must be evaluated only for their contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should follow the Reviewer Instructions which elaborate on focusing on content rather than irrelevant attributes of authors or institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prudence / flagging reasons for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must bring to the handling Area Chair any information that may be a reason to reject a submitted paper, such as violations of these guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If in doubt about issues that could affect acceptability, notify the Area Chair rather than making assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict disclosure and recusal for program committee members
rubrics_metrics.description: Program committee members must disclose conflicts via OpenReview (or by notifying the relevant AC/SAC) and cannot participate in decisions for conflicted papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program Chairs are not exempt; if a Program Chair is conflicted, non-conflicted Program Chairs must handle decisions without the conflicted chair's involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM use by reviewers and program committee
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must follow the Policy for LLM use in reviewing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the separate Policy for LLM use in reviewing for specifics (this page requires compliance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewers/Area Chairs who are also authors: duty obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: If reviewers or Area Chairs who are also authors neglect reviewing or meta-reviewing duties, all submissions on which they are authors might be desk rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of neglect include failure to communicate in a timely manner, failure to meet deadlines (without prior arrangements), violation of the LLM policy, and submission of low-quality reviews or meta-reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting alleged ethical violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspected unethical conduct should be reported to ICML via the Ethics Violation Reporting form or by emailing program-chairs@icml.cc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All suspected behaviors will be investigated by program chairs, the integrity chair, or the ICML Oversight Committee. Individuals found violating rules may face sanctions and/or have submissions rejected. ICML will collect names of individuals found violating standards and may share that list with other conferences/journals when requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with Call for Papers / Author Instructions / Peer-review Ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation of requirements in the Call for Papers, Author Instructions, or Peer-review Ethics may be grounds for desk rejection of a single submission or of all submissions by the same author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adherence to formatting, anonymity, page limits, and other procedural requirements is mandatory; see those documents for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for desk rejection of an individual submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific non-exhaustive grounds include placeholder abstracts at abstract submission, large differences between abstract and full-paper submissions, exceeding page limit, paper formatting violations, violations of author anonymity, violations of the dual submission policy (submitting papers also under review/accepted elsewhere), and hallucinated references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are examples (but not limited to) reasons an individual submission may be desk rejected; authors should ensure compliance with submission requirements and integrity standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for desk rejection of all submissions by the same author
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples include prompt injection (regardless of coauthor knowledge), violation of the concurrent submission policy (not citing/discussing concurrent ICML submissions on related topics with overlapping authors), neglect of reviewer/meta-reviewer duties (including reciprocal reviewing), and interference with the integrity of peer review (collusion, unsubstantiated conflict declarations, submission of AI slop, attempts to uncover reviewer identities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such severe violations may lead to rejection of all submissions by the same author and to other sanctions; program chairs will investigate and enforce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions and record-keeping
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigations of suspected unethical behaviors can lead to sanctions and rejected submissions; ICML will collect names of individuals found violating standards and may share this information with other conferences or journals upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting channels include the ethics form and program-chairs email; investigations are handled by program chairs, the integrity chair, or the Oversight Committee.
